title: Changed, repeated, deleted
brief: Documents change, events arrive twice, sources delete files without telling anyone, and the embedding model will change next year. Make the index tell the truth about the source, and say how you would prove it.

blocks.text: Detect: what each source can and cannot tell you

blocks.md: An index is only as true as its change and delete signals. Topics `w03-t06` (incremental ingestion), `w03-t07` (CDC and events), `w03-t08` (idempotency and hashing) and `w03-t09` (deletes, versioning, re-embedding) give the mechanisms. The matrix below is the part interviewers probe: for each source, what is seen, what is invisible and what breaks silently.

blocks.caption: Change and delete signals by source
head: Source and mode
Change signal
Delete signal
Trap
rows: Blob and ADLS Gen2 indexer
Blob `LastModified`, built in
None by default. Native blob soft delete (blob versioning off) or a metadata flag such as `IsDeleted=true`, then a physical delete
The policy must exist from the first run. A restored blob or a renamed ADLS directory is not re-indexed because `LastModified` does not change [[r4]]
Azure SQL indexer
`SqlIntegratedChangeTrackingPolicy` (tables only) or `HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy` on a `rowversion` or updated column
Change tracking sees deleted rows. Otherwise `SoftDeleteColumnDeletionDetectionPolicy` with `softDeleteColumnName`
Integrated change tracking is for tables, so a view needs the high water mark policy [[r5]]
Cosmos DB for NoSQL indexer
`HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy` on `_ts`
A top-level Boolean soft-delete field such as `IsDeleted` and a `dataDeletionDetectionPolicy`
Hard deletes are never seen [[r6]]
Cosmos DB change feed, latest version
Creates and updates, only the latest change per item
Not captured. Use a soft-delete flag plus TTL
No intermediate changes, no filter by operation type, no fixed retention [[r23]]
Cosmos DB change feed, all versions and deletes
Every create, update and delete in order, with change-type metadata
Captured, including TTL deletes
Needs continuous backup and an opt-in flag, reads only inside the backup retention window, starts only at the current time or a checkpoint [[r23]]
SharePoint indexer (preview)
The next scheduled run
Deleted files, list items and pages are detected on the next run
Preview. User-delegated tokens expire every 75 minutes, and password-protected files are not supported [[r7]]

blocks.text: Repeat and swap: safe writes and zero-downtime re-embedding

blocks.title: An idempotent ingest step (sketch, not a specific SDK)
blocks.caption: The ids come from the source id and chunk position, the fingerprint includes everything that changes the output, and the state write comes last.

blocks.title: Blue-green index behind an alias
blocks.alt: The application queries an alias that points at the old index. A pipeline fills a new index with the new embedding model. After a recall comparison on labelled queries passes, the alias is repointed to the new index, and the old index is kept for a rollback window.
blocks.src:
flowchart LR
  APP[Application] --> AL[Alias]
  AL --> BLUE[Index v1 old model]
  PIPE[Re-embed pipeline] --> GREEN[Index v2 new model]
  GREEN --> EVAL[Compare recall on labelled queries]
  EVAL -->|pass| SW[Repoint alias to v2]
  SW --> AL
  BLUE --> KEEP[Keep for rollback window]
blocks.caption: Vectors from different models are not comparable and Azure OpenAI embeddings cannot be upgraded in place, so a new index with new vector fields is the safe path [[r34]].

items.symptom: A deleted file still answers questions
items.cause: Blob and Cosmos DB indexers do not see hard deletes, and the policy must exist from the first run [[r4]] [[r6]].
items.fix: Enable a soft-delete policy, remove the orphans by key, and run a reconciliation job that lists source ids and compares them with index keys.

items.symptom: A restored file or renamed folder never comes back
items.cause: `LastModified` does not change on a restore or an ADLS Gen2 directory rename [[r4]].
items.fix: Touch the blob or reset the affected documents, and put restore and rename in your delete tests.

items.symptom: Chunks of a deleted parent linger in the index
items.cause: Index projections remove child chunks only when the data source has a deletion detection policy [[r10]].
items.fix: Add the policy, then alert on chunks whose `parent_id` is missing from the source.

items.symptom: An old version overwrites a newer one
items.cause: Delivery is at least once and not ordered: items in one Cosmos DB transactional batch share a modification time and may arrive in any order [[r23]] [[r24]] [[r25]].
items.fix: Carry a version or modified time on each event and write only when it is newer than the stored one.

items.symptom: Search returns nonsense right after an embedding model change
items.cause: New queries are embedded by one model and old vectors by another.
items.fix: Build the new index beside the old one and cut over by alias, never edit vectors in place.

blocks.title: Replay controls, checked 2026-10-13
blocks.md: Reset Indexer is GA and re-runs everything. Reset Documents, Reset Skills and Resync are preview APIs in `2026-08-01-preview` [[r8]]. An alias is a service-level resource, and the Serverless Developer tier does not support aliases [[r9]].

quiz.q: A blob indexer has run nightly for months. A user deleted a policy PDF last week, yet the assistant still cites it. No deletion detection policy was ever set. What is the right fix?
options: Run Reset Indexer, which will notice that the blob is gone and remove its chunks
Shorten the schedule to every 5 minutes so that the delete is seen much sooner
Raise `maxFailedItems` so that the missing blob stops being counted as a failure
Delete the orphan by key, turn on soft delete, and reconcile ids with the index
quiz.explain: The indexer cannot see a hard delete at any schedule, and a reset re-reads only blobs that still exist, so the orphan stays. The policy has to exist before the delete happens, and a reconciliation job is the safety net for anything the policy misses. `maxFailedItems` governs failures, not missing sources [[r4]].

quiz.q: Put the steps of a zero-downtime embedding model migration in order.
items: Create a new index with vector fields sized for the new model
Re-embed the corpus into it while the old index keeps serving
Run the labelled queries on both and compare recall
Repoint the alias to the new index
Keep the old index for a rollback window, then delete it
quiz.explain: The new index must exist before it can be filled, and it is validated before any user sees it. The alias switch is the instant cutover, and the old index is your rollback until the window passes. Because the two models' vectors cannot be mixed, there is no in-place shortcut [[r9]] [[r34]].

quiz.q: You feed a pipeline from the Cosmos DB change feed. Select the statements that are true.
options: Latest version mode does not capture deletes, so use a soft-delete flag plus TTL
All versions and deletes mode can be read only within the continuous backup retention window
Latest version mode records every intermediate update of an item
Items in one transactional batch share a modification time and may arrive in any order
quiz.explain: Latest version mode keeps only the most recent change per item and misses deletes, all versions and deletes mode needs continuous backup and has a retention window, and batch items are unordered. So the third option is false, and the consumer must tolerate gaps and reordering [[r23]].

takeaways: Know the delete story per source: Blob and Cosmos DB indexers need a soft-delete policy from day one, and hard deletes need reconciliation
Make every write idempotent: stable ids, a fingerprint that includes parser, chunker and model, and a state write last
At-least-once delivery means duplicates and reordering, so carry a version and write only newer data
Re-embed into a new index and cut over by alias, and keep the old one for a rollback window
